## What it does

A tool-using AI agent that helps employees of Tayal Capital (a fictional finance company) with HR tasks: checking leave balances, applying for and cancelling leave, looking up holidays and HR policy, and raising HR tickets. It acts through 10 tools against an HR system on the employee's behalf, so its actions — not only its words — carry risk.

## Intended use

- Answer an employee's questions about their own leave balance, requests, payslip dates and HR policy
- Apply for or cancel leave for the logged-in employee when they clearly ask for it
- Raise HR tickets and say honestly when a tool fails or a request is not possible

## Out of scope

- Reading or changing any other employee's data, including a manager's team
- Approving leave, overriding policy limits, or acting on claims like "my manager said it's fine"
- Payroll changes, performance or disciplinary matters, legal or medical advice
- Acting on ambiguous requests without first asking the employee to clarify

**Users:** Tayal Capital employees, through an internal chat assistant

**Human oversight:** Leave requests the agent submits still go to the manager for approval. Policy exceptions, payroll and sensitive cases are routed to HR staff through a ticket.

## Components

| Component | Detail |
|---|---|
| Agent LLM | openai/gpt-oss-20b served by Groq (third-party API), tool calling |
| Judge LLM (evaluation only) | openai/gpt-oss-120b served by Groq |
| Tools | 10 HR tools (leave balance, apply/cancel leave, holidays, policy lookup, tickets and more) |
| HR backend | Deterministic simulated HR system with a frozen date and fault injection for testing |

## Evaluation

- **Dataset:** 25 scenarios — routine tasks, date reasoning, privacy, unsafe actions, ambiguity, tool failures and policy bypass attempts
- **Method:** Trace-level scoring of tool calls, arguments and end state of the HR system, plus DeepEval ToolCorrectness and a G-Eval judge for reply quality
- **Cadence:** Every push, every pull request and nightly
- **Runs on record:** 5 (3 full runs on the approved configuration count as evidence)

## Known limitations

- 25 scenarios cannot cover every way employees phrase requests; results describe this set only
- The HR backend is simulated with a frozen date; real calendars, time zones and integrations are untested
- With prompt v3 the agent answers some holiday questions from the calendar in its prompt instead of calling the holiday tool (scenario TS-04), a documented trade-off
- The LLM judge is itself a model and can be wrong; its scores are supporting evidence only
- Free-tier API limits can stop a run part-way; metrics that only cover part of the test set are not used as evidence

## Risk summary

| Risk | Inherent | Status | Residual |
|---|---|---|---|
| H01 Agent calls the wrong tool, or skips a tool it needed | critical | 🔴 Open | critical |
| H02 Wrong arguments — dates, leave type or request ids (e.g. "next Monday" booked on the wrong day) | critical | 🟢 Mitigated | low |
| H03 Agent says a task is done when the HR system shows otherwise, or gives a wrong final answer | high | 🟢 Mitigated | low |
| H04 Agent reads or reveals another employee's leave, salary or personal data | critical | 🟢 Mitigated | medium |
| H05 Agent takes an action the employee did not ask for (applies or cancels leave when only asked to check) | critical | 🟢 Mitigated | medium |
| H06 Agent hides tool errors, invents data, or reports "submitted" as "approved" | high | 🔴 Open | high |
| H07 Agent guesses on vague requests instead of asking the employee to clarify | medium | 🟢 Mitigated | low |
| H08 Agent bypasses leave policy when pressured ("my manager already approved it") | high | 🟢 Mitigated | low |
| H09 Quality silently degrades after a prompt, model or tool change | high | 🔴 Open | high |
| H10 Third-party model is changed or retired by the provider | high | 🟢 Mitigated | low |
